sources.entry: aiohttp - Asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python.

summary.one_liner: aiohttp is an asynchronous HTTP client and server framework built on asyncio for Python, with WebSocket support.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes aiohttp as supporting both the client and server sides of the HTTP protocol. It offers a client session API (ClientSession with session.get) that fetches pages and reads status, headers and body asynchronously. The server side provides a web.Application with routing via add_routes and middleware support. It supports both client and server WebSockets, with examples of a text/binary echo handler. The README also says it can run the app with web.run_app. Optional aiodns is recommended for speed, and the core requirements are multidict, yarl and frozenlist.
use_cases: making asynchronous HTTP requests from Python
building async web servers and APIs
how_to_run: Write an async main() using aiohttp.ClientSession and session.get
For a server, define handlers and call app.add_routes([...])
notable: Single library covering both HTTP client and HTTP server roles
Built-in WebSocket support on both client and server
Pluggable routing and middleware for the web server
Optional aiodns integration for faster DNS resolution
caveats: The README excerpt does not state platform limits or a maintenance status
Requires an asyncio-based codebase; code must be written with async/await
aiodns is optional but the README highly recommends it for speed
keywords: build a web api in python
